title: Behavioral regression sentinel for staged rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently rely on ad-hoc golden-prompt checks and human review during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. This yields slow detection of subtle behavioral regressions (style drift, refusal-curve changes, increased hallucination on specific prompt families) and inconsistent rollback behavior across teams.

Proposal: Implement a Behavioral Regression Sentinel (BRS) that ties structured eval scorecards (families of eval prompts + metric hooks) into the rollout orchestrator. The BRS will: 1) ingest streaming responses from canary/A-B/shadow traffic, 2) compute per-prompt-family scorecards (accuracy, semantic similarity, toxic-score, hallucination heuristics, latency percentiles), 3) compare to bootstrapped baselines using robust statistical tests and bootstrapped confidence intervals, 4) produce composite degradation signals with severity scoring, and 5) expose a policy API for the rollout engine to act on (monitor-only, gated, automatic pause, or auto-rollback).

Key differentiators vs existing checks: adaptive thresholds per prompt family and per-customer (not global fixed deltas), multi-metric composite alarms (not single-metric triggers), and explicit hysteresis and grace windows to avoid noisy flips. BRS should be model-agnostic and pluggable into hosted, dedicated, and private control planes via the existing rollout webhooks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict thresholds reduce false negatives but cause more false positives; we favor an initial conservative posture (monitor-only) and escalate to auto-block after tuning.
- Per-customer baselines increase calibration complexity but reduce customer-facing churn; we will phase per-customer models after global baseline stabilizes.
- Running heavy evals inline increases latency; the design will run lightweight checks on the request path and async heavy probes on sampled traffic.

Out of scope: model retraining, long-term model improvement experiments, and correctness labeling pipelines (we will accept labeled eval sets from other teams).
acceptance_criteria: BRS service deployed in staging and receiving sampled shadow/canary traffic
Scorecards computed for at least 5 distinct eval prompt families with metrics: semantic-similarity (embedding-based), hallucination heuristics, toxicity, latency p95
Composite degradation signal generated and visible in the rollout console for canary jobs
Policy API supports monitor-only, gate (block further rollouts), and auto-rollback actions; at least monitor-only and gate are wired into the orchestrator
Alerting runbook created and Grafana dashboard linked; false-positive rate < 10% after initial tuning on internal traffic
E2E test that simulates a synthetic regression (perturbation in responses) and verifies that BRS raises expected alarm and that orchestrator pauses the canary
implementation_notes: Collector: lightweight sidecar that samples 1-5% of traffic for production canaries and all shadowed requests; attaches prompt-family tags from rollout metadata
Scorecard worker: batch compute embedding-similarity, run toxicity classifier, latency aggregation; store results in time-series DB
Baseline service: compute bootstrapped baselines per prompt-family and per-customer (start with global baselines, flag customer-level when sample size > 1000)
Policy engine: declarative rules with hysteresis windows and composite scoring; exposes REST webhook used by rollout orchestrator
Orchestrator integration: add BRS webhook target with fallback hierarchy (monitor->gate->rollback), ensure idempotency and safety checks
Phased rollout: staging monitor-only -> internal prod monitor-only for 2 weeks -> gate enabled for low-risk teams -> auto-rollback enabled behind an opt-in flag
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computations (embedding similarity, bootstrap CI), target > 90% coverage
Integration tests: end-to-end flow from collector -> scorecard -> policy decision using synthetic golden sets
Synthetic regression harness: ability to flip a golden prompt family to a perturbed model to validate detection and orchestrator action
Load test the collector and scorecard pipeline at 2x expected sample rate (simulate bursts during large canaries)
Privacy check: ensure no PII persisted in scorecard outputs and that customer opt-out is respected
